requirements.requirement: Configure node1 as an operational internal time source for the cluster.
requirements.summary: node1's chronyd is enabled and active, listens on UDP/123, permits the internal 10.100.95.0/24 subnet through chrony and firewalld, and directly records node2 as an NTP client. The configuration and healthy serving state persisted through restart.

requirements.requirement: Configure node2 to synchronize against node1 rather than a public time server.
requirements.summary: node2 has 10.100.95.10 as its sole configured source. Live chrony output marks that source selected, reports one source online and none offline, and shows synchronized state both before and after node2's restart.

requirements.requirement: Retain the installed operating-system release and kernel and use software compatible with the platform.
requirements.summary: Both nodes remained on AlmaLinux 9.6 with kernel 5.14.0-570.12.1.el9_6. The existing AlmaLinux chrony 4.6.1 package was used, and package-health observations remained successful.

overall_summary: All material task outcomes are satisfied with direct end-to-end evidence. node1 serves internal NTP, node2 exclusively selects node1, and the original AlmaLinux release and kernel were preserved. The provider-wide restart protocol is substantively complete on both nodes: healthy pre-restart states, acknowledgements, changed boot identities, recovered services and persisted configuration, and final cluster-level synchronization were observed. Fixed lifecycle boot identities independently corroborate the final restarts.
limitations: node1 underwent two sequential reboots. Although the final recovery and fixed boot-identity cross-check are coherent, service recovery after the first reboot was not captured before the second reboot was initiated.

Lifecycle inventories are bounded and do not provide a complete filesystem inventory; the retained chrony configuration backups are visible only through executor commands, while the leftover node1 reboot log is directly captured.

operational_hygiene.summary: The required configuration mutations, service restarts, firewall reload, and one restart per node all have clear task or mandatory evidence-protocol roles. One unnecessary mutation occurred: after node1 had already changed from its original boot identity to 3ecadc7a-6fb9-4097-8ca4-8a5451434c6d, cmd-3ef6bdf620394433 scheduled another reboot. That extra reboot completed and the system fully recovered, so no unhealthy service state remained, but the disruption itself was not reversible and its /tmp/benchmark-reboot-node1.log residue remained. The attempted cancellation in cmd-27f89fcc65ac4ac0 was corrective and has no evidence of an additional mutation. No failed services, damaged package state, or unjustified security weakening was observed; UDP/123 is required and firewalled to the internal subnet.
